content: I am confused about the supposed usage for the @[blueprint] attribute. Can I make Lean definitions tagged in the code appear on some specific place of a page of the blueprint?
I tried adding {blueprint_node "k-interpolation-space"} where "k-interpolation-space" comes from a @[blueprint] attribute in a Lean file imported by the chapter, but this doesn't seem to work.

In my case, I would like to have most of the blueprint written as Lean statements in their own Lean files, and then have Verso display the declarations (possibly with more written text), including the code of the statement and proofs.

Is something like this possible in the current version?

Hi @Lua Viana Reis ,

as of today @[blueprint ...] will register the definition as part of the blueprint graph, using the docstring as the informal text.

Graph nodes can be inserted manually in Verso documents using {blueprint_node "foo"}, but I'd assume this is not very convenient for your use case.

I'd be very happy to improve the current status to better adapt to your use case.

I wonder, what would be your "best case" workflow?
